title: Polio left her unable to walk at 14. She built a literacy movement from her wheelchair instead. October 10, 2026.
excerpt: From a Nobel Peace Prize shared across a border, to a chip plant shipping its first US export, October 10's five stories are about work that scales past the person or place that started it.
bodyHtml:
Every story today is about something that outgrew its own starting point - a prize shared across a hostile border, a DNA-sequencing method that became global infrastructure, a telemedicine model that circled back to its founder's home state, a second chip plant turning a single factory into a pattern, and a literacy movement built from a wheelchair that outlived the woman who started it.

October 10, 2014: India got its first Nobel Peace Prize - shared with a 17-year-old from Pakistan

Kailash Satyarthi and Malala Yousafzai were named joint winners of the 2014 Nobel Peace Prize for their fight against child labour and for every child's right to education - Satyarthi becoming the first Indian-born person to win it, deliberately paired with a Pakistani laureate for the same cause.

He invented the DNA sequencing method that made a $200 human genome possible. It just won him a Wolf Prize

Shankar Balasubramanian won the 2026 Wolf Prize in Chemistry for inventing the Solexa/Illumina next-generation DNA sequencing method - technology that cut genome sequencing costs roughly a million-fold and now underlies most of the world's genomic medicine.

His free video-call training model raised one state's hepatitis-C diagnosis 100x

Dr. Sanjeev Arora founded Project ECHO in New Mexico in 2003 to train rural doctors via videoconferencing instead of flying in specialists. The model returned to his home state as ECHO India, raising Punjab's hepatitis-C diagnosis from roughly 1,500 to 150,000 patients.

India just shipped its first chip export to a US power semiconductor company

Kaynes Semicon's Rs 3,300 crore OSAT facility at Sanand, Gujarat - India's second semiconductor plant to open there within a month - shipped its first commercial Intelligent Power Modules to California-based Alpha and Omega Semiconductor.

Polio left her unable to walk at 14. She built a literacy movement from her wheelchair instead

K. V. Rabiya, struck by polio as a teenager in Kerala, launched a grassroots adult-literacy campaign in 1992 and founded the volunteer organization 'Chalanam.' She received the Padma Shri in 2022 and passed away in May 2025, mourned nationally.

Five stories, one thread: a prize that crossed a border, a lab discovery that became world infrastructure, a telemedicine model that came home to help its founder's own state, a chip plant that turned into a trend, and a movement that outgrew the woman who built it from a wheelchair. Nothing here stayed small.
